# Challenge: Async Event Bus — DLQ Redelivery & Regex Subscriptions

The pub/sub broker has two defects:

1. `broker.py`: subscriber exceptions propagate out of `publish()`; failed
   dispatches are never retried and never reach the Dead Letter Queue.
2. `broker.py`: `subscribe_regex()` stores its pattern as a literal topic
   string, so regex subscriptions never match.

Fix both defects. Do not modify the test suite.

import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from bus import Broker, Subscription


def test_dead_letter_queue_redelivery():
    broker = Broker()
    calls = {"flaky": 0}

    def flaky(topic, payload):
        calls["flaky"] += 1
        if calls["flaky"] <= 2:
            raise RuntimeError("transient failure")

    def reliable(topic, payload):
        reliable.received = True

    broker.subscribe(Subscription("orders.*", flaky, retries=3))
    broker.subscribe(Subscription("orders.*", reliable, retries=0))
    broker.publish("orders.created", {"id": 7})  # must not raise
    assert calls["flaky"] == 3  # two failures then one successful redelivery
    assert reliable.received
    assert broker.dlq == []

    def hopeless(topic, payload):
        raise RuntimeError("permanent failure")

    broker.subscribe(Subscription("billing.*", hopeless, retries=1))
    broker.publish("billing.charge", {"amount": 10})
    assert len(broker.dlq) == 1
    assert broker.dlq[0][0] == "billing.charge"
    assert broker.dlq[0][1] == {"amount": 10}


def test_regex_topic_matching():
    broker = Broker()
    received = []

    def cb(topic, payload):
        received.append((topic, payload))

    broker.subscribe_regex(r"order\.[0-9]+\.created", cb)
    broker.publish("order.42.created", {"total": 5})
    assert received and received[0][1] == {"total": 5}
    broker.publish("order.XX.created", {"bad": 1})
    assert len(received) == 1  # non-matching topic stays unmatched


def test_direct_topic_publish():
    broker = Broker()
    got = []
    broker.subscribe(Subscription("metrics.cpu", lambda t, p: got.append((t, p))))
    broker.publish("metrics.cpu", 0.75)
    assert got == [("metrics.cpu", 0.75)]


def test_wildcard_unsubscribe():
    broker = Broker()
    got = []
    sub = Subscription("logs.*", lambda t, p: got.append(t))
    broker.subscribe(sub)
    broker.publish("logs.app", "hello")
    assert got == ["logs.app"]
    broker.unsubscribe(sub)
    broker.publish("logs.app", "world")
    assert len(got) == 1
